$comment: The permission profile every Claude Eindri is launched with (plan 239 P5c). A worker runs unattended in its own Yggdrasil worktree, so it may edit and run commands without a prompt (the same latitude opencode workers get from OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT permission *:allow), while the moves that only the Allfather makes, or that destroy unrecorded work, are denied. Deny rules win over allow rules. Appended 2026-11-20: the seat runs in dontAsk mode, so a tool outside this allow list is denied, never asked about; bin/seat/claude-seat.sh adds one allow per configured MCP server at launch. THE COMMAND TIME LIMIT (2026-11-20, "yes not to small tho"): a Bash call defaults to 2 minutes and may declare at most 10, which is short enough that a real build is killed and long enough that a hung ssh hides for hours. 30 minutes by default, 2 hours when a build or a gate suite declares it, never unlimited — the same numbers as bin/agents/cmd-limit-lib.sh, which is where the brief rule and the arm's judgement read them. Appended 2026-11-21 (RULES/08, every PR is reviewed by the judge and an approval merges at once): THE PROFILE IS CHOSEN BY ROLE (src/ymir_runtime/claude_seat.py profile_for). This is the WORKER profile: a worker never merges by any road, so besides raw `gh pr merge` and `git merge` it also refuses the judge's merge door (bin/forge/judge-merge.sh, bin/agents/pr-seal.sh seal) and the raw merge API. The judge (role forseti) is seated with claude-judge.settings.json instead, which opens the door and nothing else. Appended 2026-11-21 (the judge's review of #870): raw merge also hides behind gh's global flags (`gh -R <repo> pr merge`) and the GraphQL mutation (`mergePullRequest`); both are denied here and refused by the smith gh shim. Appended later the same day (the judge's re-review): `-R/--repo` may also stand BETWEEN `pr` and `merge` (`gh pr -R <repo> merge`), an alias can carry a merge, and the API path may end in a slash or change case; all are denied here and refused by the shim, which reads the subcommand past every flag, judges an alias by its expansion and matches the API path without case. A pattern list cannot fence a Bash that is open: the lasting fence is a judge-only token.
